package_info.package_name: UI Automation Attack Tool (generic, PoC or custom malware)
package_info.package_versions: All Windows versions since XP (no package version, but all OS versions affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The tool abuses the legitimate UI Automation framework to stealthily monitor, manipulate, and exfiltrate sensitive user data from other applications, bypassing EDR detection. It leverages elevated UI interaction permissions to harvest credentials, credit card data, and perform unauthorized actions in user sessions, representing a significant threat to user privacy and system integrity.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user launches the malicious program
execution_context.file_location: Malicious EXE or script (invokes UIAutomationCore.dll via COM API)
required_permissions: Read/write access to other process UI elements

malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (or any language supporting COM/Win32 API)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initializes the UI Automation COM object, creates an instance of the UIAutomation interface, and registers a global event handler to monitor UI element changes in other applications, enabling real-time surveillance of sensitive user actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registering global UI Automation event handlers to monitor other processes' UI activity is highly unusual outside of accessibility tools, and is a common technique for surveillance and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not create global UI Automation handlers targeting external processes unless they are legitimate accessibility tools; malware does so to spy on user activity without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Screen readers or accessibility tools for users with disabilities may use similar APIs, but are typically signed, well-known, and do not operate covertly.
key_indicators: AddEventHandler targeting windows or controls in external processes
Global event handler registration outside accessibility context

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, upon a monitored UI event (e.g., user enters data in a browser or chat application)
execution_context.file_location: Event handler callback within the malicious binary
required_permissions: Read access to UI element properties
Network access (for exfiltration of captured data)

malicious_snippets.code_language: C++/C#/Python (pseudo-code, matches UI Automation API usage)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a monitored UI element changes, such as a credit card input field, the event handler reads the new value from the UI element and immediately sends the captured data to an external server, enabling real-time credential or financial data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reading sensitive UI fields and exfiltrating their contents to an external server is a hallmark of spyware and credential-stealing malware, not legitimate accessibility behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Accessibility tools may read field values for speech output or assistive purposes, but should never transmit sensitive data externally or log it for unauthorized use.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility tools may read field values for local speech output or display, but do not exfiltrate or store sensitive data.
key_indicators: get_CurrentName() or get_CurrentValue() calls on sensitive fields (e.g., 'Credit Card Number')
Immediate network exfiltration of UI element data after user input
Event handler logic that filters for credential or payment fields

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after locating a target UI element (e.g., chat input or browser form) via UI Automation tree traversal
execution_context.file_location: Malicious binary, after traversing the UI element tree
required_permissions: Write access to UI elements in other processes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after identifying a target UI element such as a chat input field, the code programmatically writes a malicious message or command into the field, enabling message injection or unauthorized command execution in user applications.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Programmatic manipulation of UI elements in other applications is rarely legitimate and is a common technique for automation-based attacks, such as message injection or command execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not inject messages or commands into other applications' UI elements without explicit user consent or a clear accessibility purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated testing tools or accessibility input aids may write to UI elements, but are typically used in controlled environments and do not target user sessions covertly.
key_indicators: setValue or equivalent write operations on UI elements in external processes
Targeting of chat, browser, or credential input fields for injection
Automated input into user-facing applications outside of testing or accessibility contexts

attack_chain.action: Initialize the UI Automation COM object and register global event handlers to monitor UI changes in other applications.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables real-time observation of sensitive user actions across multiple applications.

attack_chain.action: Filter and process UI events to identify when sensitive data, such as credit card information or chat messages, is entered by the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: Harvests sensitive data from user sessions for potential theft.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrate harvested data to an attacker-controlled server or inject malicious input into target applications via UI element manipulation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Results in data theft, account compromise, or further attack propagation through message injection.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual use of UIAutomationCore.dll by non-accessibility or unsigned applications
Processes registering global UI Automation event handlers targeting external processes
Accessing or modifying UI elements in other processes outside of accessibility or testing contexts
Network activity (e.g., outbound connections) immediately following sensitive UI events such as credential or payment field entry
file_indicators: Presence of binaries or scripts importing or dynamically loading UIAutomationCore.dll
Unexpected creation of UI Automation named pipes (e.g., \\.\pipe\UIA_PIPE_*)
Unsigned or unknown executables invoking UI Automation APIs
network_indicators: Outbound connections to external IPs or domains immediately after sensitive UI activity (e.g., credit card entry)
Exfiltration of UI element data to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credential or payment data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for non-accessibility processes loading UIAutomationCore.dll and registering global event handlers. Flag processes that access or modify UI elements in other applications, especially if followed by network activity. Watch for creation of unexpected UI Automation named pipes (e.g., \\.\pipe\UIA_PIPE_*). Correlate UI event monitoring with outbound network connections to detect exfiltration attempts. Prioritize detection on unsigned or unknown binaries exhibiting these behaviors.
